title: Standalone Invocation
BeadsAdapter.createEpic delegates to the read-only FileAdapter, so epics can never exist on the beads backend
description: Found 2026-08-13 immediately after fixing issue-626 (the --db path bug) and retrying 'adev issues migrate --to beads --include-closed' on this repo. SECOND, INDEPENDENT blocker -- structural, not a config or path problem. beads-adapter.mjs:241 has createEpic() delegate unconditionally to this._fileAdapter.createEpic(), and file-adapter.mjs:133-135 is 'async createEpic(_epicData) { throw deprecatedWrite(); }' -- an unconditional throw, because the file (markdown) backend is read-only by design. So epic creation on the beads backend is impossible by construction. The adapter's own header comment states the intent: 'Epic operations are delegated to a FileAdapter instance since beads_rust has no epic concept (hybrid approach per SA-5)' -- but the adapter chosen to hold them cannot be written to, so the hybrid has no writable home for epics. OBSERVED RESULT of the retry: all 308 issues migrated successfully and .beads-map.json holds 308 entries (verified directly: 'br --db .beads/beads.db list --json' returns 308), then the run aborted at index 308 -- the FIRST epic, epic-1 -- with 'The file (markdown) backend is read-only.' So 0 of 106 epics and 0 of 41 dependency edges migrated. Epic MEMBERSHIP does survive: 242 of the 308 map entries carry epicId metadata, consistent with backend-adapters.spec.md:49 which says epicId/planRef filters read from .beads-map.json because beads does not track them natively. What is missing is the epic ENTITIES (title, status, milestone) and every dependency edge. SECOND DEFECT observed in the same run: the migrate verb reported created:{issues:0,epics:0} even though 308 issues were demonstrably created -- the counter is not incremented before the abort, so a partially-successful run reports as a total no-op and understates what actually landed. That is dangerous on its own: a re-run looks safe when it is not. (It is in fact idempotent via .beads-map.json, but the report gives no way to know that.) NOTE ON API GENERATION: createEpic emits 'createEpic is deprecated; use create() instead. See task-management charter rev 3' under ADEV_DEPRECATION_WARN=1, so the migrate verb drives a deprecated path. Any fix should decide how epics are represented under beads at all -- most plausibly as tiered issues via the unified create() rather than as a separate entity class -- which is a design decision, not a patch. CURRENT STATE, nothing is live: manifest still reads tasks.backend: json, the json board remains authoritative and complete at 308 issues / 106 epics, and the populated .beads store plus .beads-map.json are present but unwired. Pre-migration snapshot committed at c3d4a875 on branch chore/board-migrate-to-beads.; Closed: ALREADY FIXED ON MAIN. Commit 9dc95701 identified the same root cause ("Epics were delegated to FileAdapter, which is read-only-deprecated, so createEpic threw BACKEND_READ_ONLY_DEPRECATED"), and dcb4f591 ("make beads the single source of truth — delete the sidecar") went further than this issue proposed: it removed .beads-map.json entirely, storing adev ids in br external_ref, metadata in br agent_context, and epics as br issues with issue_type: epic. That is the same charter-derived conclusion this issue reached (an epic is a root-level WorkItem, not a separate entity) but implemented without a second store that can disagree. A local fix was written independently (commit 34a5c685, 8 TDD tests) and is DISCARDED as redundant; reflog only. Verified fixed: migration against main creates 106 epic-* external_refs with 0 errors. Also note the created-counter misreporting flagged here is still live on main -- a run that demonstrably created 106 epics reported created:{epics:0}, skipped:106. Rolled into issue-628.

title: Retire the 83 prose-matching test files once tier-2 diagnostics replace them
description: The missing BACKFILL half of issue-557. 557 builds the replacement (tier-2 diagnostic producers for SKILL.md/spec/docs structure) and forbids string-matching prose as a future test deliverable — but it does not touch the existing corpus. Nothing on the board currently migrates or retires it, so without this issue adev would ship the new mechanism while keeping ~10k lines of the old pattern in the suite indefinitely. Found 2026-08-13 when the gap was queried directly; the orchestrator had previously and incorrectly assumed 557 covered remediation. Scale (2026-08-10 audit): ~27% of this repo's test CASES are change-detectors; 103 files import NO production code and only readFileSync a .md and call .includes(). tests/skills/ is ~87% this pattern and tests/docs/ is 100% — together 83 files / ~10k lines / 824 cases with essentially zero production coverage. 340 assertions use the near-tautological includes(x) || includes(y) form. Precedent for the split: epic-104 separates producer fixes (issue-585 spec templates, issue-586 review/validate writer) from the backfill of ~400 existing artifacts (issue-587). epic-108 had the producer half (557) and was missing this one. HARD DEPENDENCY on issue-557: do not delete a prose test until the tier-2 producer that covers its invariant actually ships, or coverage is silently lost rather than migrated. Per-file the decision is three-way, not a blanket delete: (a) invariant now covered by a tier-2 diagnostic -> delete the test; (b) invariant real but NOT expressible as a diagnostic -> rewrite as a behavioral test that imports production code; (c) assertion was tautological (the includes(x) || includes(y) family) -> delete outright, it never tested anything. Requires a per-file audit; the count of files deleted vs rewritten vs dropped should be reported, since 'deleted 83 files' and 'migrated 83 invariants' are very different outcomes. Interacts with issue-555 (its hygiene test-debt pass detects prose-assertion density, so it can measure progress here) and issue-615 (cross-layer duplicate coverage — some prose tests may be duplicates rather than needing migration at all). || SCOPE ESTIMATE CONTESTED 2026-08-13 — RE-MEASURE BEFORE PLANNING. issue-555's shipped test-debt scanner (Audit Pass 23) dogfooded this repo and found PROSE_ASSERTION = 25 files, not the 83-103 this issue was filed with. The numbers measure different things and both are internally valid: 227 test files reference a .md path and 115 reference SKILL.md, but only 25 also clear the 0.5 containment-assertion ratio. The audit counted files that TOUCH markdown (specifically: import no production code and only readFileSync a .md and call .includes()); the scanner counts files whose ASSERTIONS are predominantly markdown containment. A file asserting via assert.match regex rather than .includes() lands in the audit's set but may miss the scanner's ratio. Neither is wrong; they answer different questions. Consequence for this issue: do NOT plan against either figure. Run 'adev test-debt scan' for the low-false-positive set (25), then separately enumerate the audit's criterion (no production import + markdown-only assertions) for the outer bound, and reconcile per-file — the three-way audit below is what actually decides each file, and it will resolve files the ratio heuristic misses. Also note issue-555's validate report says 'Remediation of those files is issue-557 territory' — that is the same error this issue was filed to correct; 557 builds the replacement, THIS issue retires the corpus.

title: adev gates doctor: verify declared gates actually run and tests actually get collected
description:
HIGHEST-LEVERAGE finding of the 2026-08-10 three-repo audit (adev-plugin, repo-B, repo-C accelerator). All three repos wrote tests that never executed, and adev never noticed: adev-plugin’s npm test glob silently skipped 67 files / ~1,000 cases (sh has no globstar, so tests/**/*.test.mjs == tests/*/*.test.mjs); repo-B CI ran only 19% of test files and ZERO Python tests (70k LOC, ~3,000 test fns, never run in CI); repo-C had no CI at all, pytest was not even a dependency, and its declared gates cd into a gitignored repo so they cannot execute. Root cause: adev rigorously verifies test AUTHORSHIP (RED-state verification, immutable handoff hashes, tamper detection) but never verifies test COLLECTION or EXECUTION. Proposed verb: (a) discover test files on disk, ask each runner what it collects, diff the two; (b) execute each declared gate command and confirm it can run; (c) verify CI config exists and invokes the gates; (d) flag unsubstituted {{ }} placeholders; (e) flag gate commands pointing at gitignored or nonexistent paths. Wire into /adev:validate and /adev:hygiene. Nearest existing coverage is hygiene Audit Pass 8, which checks the gate binary is on PATH but explicitly says "Do not run the command." Attach to the shipped validate check registry (.context-index/governance/validate.yaml) — no new infrastructure needed.

title: Redact out-of-repo absolute paths in session summaries
description:
Session capture writes absolute paths from unrelated repositories into committed session summaries. This is the root cause of the 2026-08-13 client-name leak into the public repo: .context-index/sessions/2026-05-27-9038da0.md and 2026-08-10-12e3fdb.md each leaked a client name through a 'Files touched:' line listing paths from other checkouts and /private/tmp scratchpads.

Fix: extend REDACTION_PATTERNS / redactSecrets() in lib/session-summary.mjs (applied unconditionally by fromTranscript) to redact absolute paths outside the repository root, emitting repo-relative paths only.

Scale evidence: during the 2026-08-14 stash rescue, 211 of 509 recovered files contained /Users/<user>/Development/<repo> absolute paths and 22 contained /private/tmp scratchpad paths. See PR #261.
close_reason: Fixed in 9fde06af. Out-of-repo absolute paths are now redacted at BOTH write chokepoints, not just the one named in the issue: fromTranscript (session-summary.mjs:536) and writeSummary (:833). That second one is what actually closes the cited 2026-08-13 leak — the leaked "Files touched:" lines are built by .githooks/post-commit:150 and written via writeSummary at :156, a path that never calls fromTranscript, so fixing only the transcript pipeline would have hardened the framework while leaving the real vector open. Design: patterns run LAST (path-first would eat the token= anchor in /Users/x/proj/token=abc123 and leave the secret exposed); prefix-scoped deny-list so /usr/bin/node survives by construction; FAILS CLOSED — a project root that is or contains homedir() is rejected so nothing is exempt. In-repo paths preserved as useful signal. 36 redaction tests, 89/89 across session-summary. Already-committed leaked files deliberately untouched — rewriting public history is a separate decision.

description:

baselined until this is repaired.

INDEPENDENTLY MEASURED 2026-08-14 (md5 + line counts, not taken from the research):

    baseline      9076b0682890ab3b90a45e80911972b6   298 lines
    conservative  04e2fee99d5d6522d80c66fb6c3a620e   216
    summarized    9076b0682890ab3b90a45e80911972b6   298   <-- IDENTICAL to baseline
    aggressive    9a8ea18c1ab166ef2afc0bc28543c5d4   179

    conservative  b5860cbaaa4f4f93c072a7417cf7585b   564
    summarized    dca561eb812c9c47613f1260d29d575a   682   <-- IDENTICAL to baseline
    aggressive    a7fd5c1fa85f6a4c9b5656775c9fbc5c   107

    baseline      a5617ab7c56055e9bb4a933a15b71a88   969 lines
    conservative  MISSING
    summarized    455812c9d20a6e31cf3cb7225e25555f  1002   <-- LARGER than baseline
    aggressive    MISSING

Of 12 matrix cells: 2 missing, 2 byte-identical to baseline, and the one genuine
"summarized" variant is BIGGER than the thing it summarises. The summarized arm
therefore has exactly zero valid cells.

Also: tests/evals/skill-compression/outputs/ does not exist. The runner globs
outputs/<variant>/<skill>/output.md and scores nothing.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN NO DATA. Capture outputs now and the summarized arm scores
identically to baseline — not because summarising preserved quality, but because
the files are the same bytes. That reads as evidence that compression is free, and
it is the baseline every skill-consolidation issue in epic-9zqjfj would be measured
against.

REPAIR ORDER:
  1. Author genuine conservative/plan.md and aggressive/plan.md.
  2. Re-author summarized/{brainstorm,specify}.md as actual summarisations.
  3. Explain or fix summarized/plan.md being larger than baseline.
  4. Add a matrix-integrity check (no two cells byte-identical; no cell missing;
     summarized < baseline by line count) so this cannot silently regress.
  5. Only then capture outputs/ and wire the deterministic layer into CI.

The harness-simplification-study flags this as unfiled work — its epic-108 /
issue-620 citations name IDs that were never allocated. This is that issue.

Method note worth keeping, from the study: that audit checked whether each harness
RAN. It did not check whether each harness's INPUTS were valid. That is a distinct
check, and it is where this defect hid.
close_reason: Fixed. All 12 matrix cells now exist, are byte-distinct, and satisfy the ordering; verified independently (0 duplicate md5s). ROOT CAUSE, which the issue did not have: commit 1166071a created summarized/{brainstorm,specify}.md as VERBATIM baseline copies — filler to make the directory look complete — and summarized/plan.md was legitimately larger because summarized was originally a DIFFERENT AXIS: output verbosity (artifact-to-disk), not prompt compression. It was baseline plus a 33-line output directive. Resolved by making the arm both — condensed body plus the artifact-to-disk directive, applied uniformly. That is also why the integrity check deliberately has no conservative-vs-summarized assertion: the two arms compress along different axes. Line counts: brainstorm 298/216/261/179, specify 682/564/262/107, plan 969/875/369/195. Beyond line counts, each rubric match_pattern set was run against every variant prompt to prove no load-bearing instruction was dropped — baked into the test as a rubric floor, because a variant missing an instruction would make the eval report an authoring bug as a quality cost of compression. Integrity check: 39/39, and re-verified it still bites (removing one cell drops it to 36/3). TWO CAVEATS RECORDED: conservative/plan.md is a weak treatment at -9.7% because plan baseline is dominated by tables and fenced blocks the conservative tier keeps by definition, so its likely parity with baseline must NOT be read as compression being free; and the summarized arm intensity varies across skills (-12.4/-61.6/-61.9%), so do not average across skills within an arm — the harness scores per-skill against per-skill rubrics, so within-skill comparison is unaffected. outputs/ deliberately not captured; baselining is the next step and is now safe to take.

title: adev install/upgrade: plugin enabled user-wide before the user/project scope prompt; domain picker runs at install instead of init
description:
The install/upgrade sequence performs two irreversible actions before (or instead of) the point at which the user gets to decide them.

DEFECT 1 — plugin is installed AND enabled user-wide before the scope prompt.
cli/index.mjs:605-615 (claude-code branch of installProviders()):
  1. `await provider.install()` is called with NO opts, so providers/claude-code/adapter.mjs:53 defaults `scope = "user"`, and adapter.mjs:85 calls `this.enable("user")` — writing `enabledPlugins["adev@agentic-development"] = true` into ~/.claude/settings.json (adapter.mjs:123-136).
  2. ONLY THEN does cli/index.mjs:613 ask "Install for all projects (user) or this project only (project)?".
  3. cli/index.mjs:614 calls `provider.enable("project")`, which writes <cwd>/.claude/settings.json — but nothing ever REMOVES the user-scope entry written in step 1.

Consequence: answering "project" does not produce a project-scoped install. The plugin stays enabled for every project on the machine, and the user is never told. The prompt is effectively cosmetic for the "project" answer.

Related: adapter.mjs:99-117 `updateRegistry()` hardcodes `scope: existing?.scope || "user"` in ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json, so a fresh install records "user" regardless of the answer.

In-repo precedent for the correct shape: the codex branch at cli/index.mjs:667-678 asks for scope FIRST, then calls `provider.install({ scope: targetScope })`. The claude-code branch should match it. (The cursor branch at cli/index.mjs:680 hardcodes `scope: "user"` with no prompt at all — worth deciding intentionally rather than leaving implicit.)

DEFECT 2 — domain-extension picker runs at install/upgrade time, not at init time.
cli/index.mjs:975 (cmdInstall) and cli/index.mjs:1128 (cmdUpgrade) both call runDomainPicker(), which installs a domain extension into the project and writes `domain: <name>` into .context-index/manifest.yaml. This happens during CLI install — before the user has run /adev:init and before any project configuration exists (install has only scaffolded pristine templates at that point). Picking a domain is a project-configuration decision and belongs with the rest of them.

Documented intent already disagrees with the wiring: lib/cli/domain-extension-picker.mjs's module header calls it the "Init-time domain-extension picker helper" while documenting cmdInstall()/cmdUpgrade() as its consumers.

Note on scope of the fix: skills/init/SKILL.md has a "Domain Extension Picker" section (~lines 950-992), but it only DOCUMENTS the picker as an `adev install`/`adev upgrade` step — /adev:init does not itself run the picker. So the fix is not merely "delete the call from install/upgrade"; it also needs a picker step added to the init flow, plus the SKILL.md section rewritten to describe init-time behavior.

SCOPE
- cli/index.mjs installProviders() claude-code branch (605-615); decide cursor branch (680) too
- providers/claude-code/adapter.mjs install()/enable()/updateRegistry() — scope must be honored end to end, including removing/never-writing the user entry when "project" is chosen
- cli/index.mjs cmdInstall() (975) and cmdUpgrade() (1128) — remove runDomainPicker()
- skills/init/SKILL.md — add the picker as an init step; rewrite the Domain Extension Picker section
- Tests for both paths (install and upgrade), asserting that answering "project" leaves ~/.claude/settings.json untouched

ACCEPTANCE
1. No user-wide write of any kind occurs before the scope answer is collected.
2. Answering "project" writes only <cwd>/.claude/settings.json; ~/.claude/settings.json gains no enabledPlugins entry for adev. (The extraKnownMarketplaces user-level write at adapter.mjs:138-172 is a separate concern — decide explicitly whether it is exempt, and document the decision.)
3. installed_plugins.json records the scope the user actually chose.
4. `adev install` and `adev upgrade` do not run the domain-extension picker.
5. /adev:init runs the picker and writes `domain:` to manifest.yaml.
6. Both defects covered by tests on the install AND upgrade paths.

Found 2026-08-14 during a walkthrough of the install/upgrade UX.

title: `adev worktree merge` reports any git failure as MERGE_CONFLICT, and aborts a clean merge
description:
ROOT CAUSE ISOLATED. `mergeWorktree` (lib/worktree.mjs:226-247) wraps `git merge`
in a try/catch that treats ANY non-zero exit as a merge conflict. The caught `err`
is never inspected — git's stderr, which carries the real reason, is discarded.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, the second worse than the first.

1. MISLEADING DIAGNOSIS. On a non-conflict failure, `git diff --diff-filter=U`
   returns nothing, so the thrown message reads:

     MERGE_CONFLICT: merge of adev/fix-513 conflicts on 0 file(s):

   A conflict on zero files is a contradiction, and it sends the operator
   looking for conflicted files that do not exist.

2. IT DISCARDS A CLEAN MERGE. Line 239 runs `git merge --abort` unconditionally
   in the catch. When the merge itself succeeded and only the COMMIT was rejected,
   the staged, conflict-free merge is thrown away. The caller is told it conflicted
   and is left with nothing.

OBSERVED LIVE 2026-08-14 merging adev/fix-513. The real cause was the commit-msg
hook rejecting the merge commit for a missing `Spec:` trailer — a hook this repo
ships and enforces on every commit, so this is not an exotic path. The merge had
no conflicts at all: retrying with plain `git merge --no-ff` produced a clean
staged merge and the hook's actual message, and completing it with a Spec: trailer
succeeded on the first try.

COST OF THE MISDIAGNOSIS: believing the verb, I ran `scripts/sync-provider-skills.mjs`
on top of what I thought was a completed merge, generating provider mirrors from
pre-merge skills that then had to be reverted.

PROPOSED FIX
  (a) Only report MERGE_CONFLICT when `--diff-filter=U` is NON-EMPTY. Otherwise
      surface the underlying git failure verbatim with a distinct code, e.g.
      MERGE_FAILED, carrying err.stderr.
  (b) Do not `merge --abort` when there are no conflicted paths. A hook-rejected
      merge is recoverable by fixing the message and committing; aborting destroys
      that. Leave the tree staged and say so.
  (c) Name the commit-msg hook case explicitly if detectable, since this repo
      requires a Spec: trailer on merge commits touching spec-manifest files —
      making it the most likely failure the verb will ever hit here.

Verified by reading lib/worktree.mjs:224-248 and reproducing both the failure and
the clean retry.

title: Author one regression rubric per skill epic-102 intends to change, BEFORE changing it
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13. 32 rubric files exist across 7 eval directories, which overstates coverage badly. Only THREE are per-skill compression-regression rubrics — tests/evals/skill-compression/rubrics/{brainstorm,plan,specify}.yaml — covering 3 of 30 skills, and one of those three (plan) sits on the broken variant matrix in issue-620. The other 29 rubrics score different things: whole-workflow scenarios (work-tracking, configurable-governance), domain-level project comparisons (comparison/), infrastructure honesty (integration-sandbox), and a data-domain set (data-engineering). A rubric that scores a six-step lifecycle scenario tells you the pipeline ran; it cannot tell you that /adev:route's scoring degraded after its prose was compressed.

THIRTEEN skills have no rubric mention at all: codehealth, deploy, init, learn, prototype, reconcile, recover, repomap, research, retro, sample, sync, using-adev.

THE OVERLAP THAT MAKES THIS URGENT: the skills epic-102 queues for demotion, merging and deletion are almost exactly the skills with no coverage. issue-573 targets codehealth, repomap, document, deploy, sync; issue-574 targets learn and issues; issue-575 merges eval into validate --score, assess into init --brownfield, and reduces using-adev; issue-576 deletes skills/standalone; issue-571 rewrites prototype. Of those, codehealth / repomap / deploy / sync / learn / using-adev / prototype / standalone have NO rubric, and issues / eval / assess / document are touched only by scenario rubrics. That is not a coincidence — they are the peripheral skills, which is both why they look expendable and why nobody built evals for them. The consequence is that the simplification sweep would run exactly where the regression net is thinnest.

SCOPE: not 30 rubrics. One rubric per skill epic-102 intends to touch — roughly 10 — each authored BEFORE that skill is modified, so the comparison is against a captured baseline rather than a memory of how it used to behave. Cheap to write: the existing scenarios (tests/evals/skill-compression/scenarios/*.md) are self-contained prompts carrying simulated user responses, so runs are reproducible without a human in the loop. Follow the existing rubric shape — regex-matched required_elements (deterministic, 50%) plus weighted quality_dimensions (50%) — with the judged half restructured into BINARY per-criterion verdicts rather than 1-5 scales, per the external research on judge reliability.

SEQUENCING: this is the real gate on epic-102, not a nice-to-have. A rubric authored after a skill is compressed measures the compressed skill against itself. Priority order should follow epic-102's own: 573 and 575 first (they touch the most skills), then 574, 571, 576.

NUANCE for issue-576 (delete skills/standalone): a deleted skill needs a different test, not a compression rubric — assert that the CLI path it wrapped still works and that no caller is stranded. Worth stating explicitly so nobody writes a rubric for a file that is about to vanish.

Reference target from the research digest: 20-50 tasks drawn from real failures, each with a reference solution, outcome-graded, held near 100% as a regression gate. Three compression rubrics is roughly a tenth of that floor.

title: /adev:route mutates plan files — sibling .routing.md fix + cursor-provider 5-plan migration
description:
Source: cursor-provider retro 2026-05-19 + /adev:debug subagent transcript (agent ID affc19ea4ef7212c7).
Consolidated re-filing after the prior issue-525 + issue-528 entries were lost in an external rollback of the shared tasks.json.

## The bug

/adev:route Step 4 (skills/route/SKILL.md:108-133) is explicitly instructed to write **Routing:** / **Scores:** / **Rationale:** blocks into each task header inside the plan markdown file. This runs AFTER /adev:plan Step 7 (skills/plan/SKILL.md:678-701) has already emitted plan_task pending events to the lifecycle log.

This directly violates the authoritative-channel invariant CON-8 in agent-reliable-state-artifacts/plan-task-events.spec.md:50-58 ("Plan markdown is read-only after authoring ... /adev:plan writes the plan file once") and AC bullet 5 ("Plan markdown files are not mutated by /adev:plan or /adev:implement after initial authoring").

The detector in lib/plan-immutability.mjs correctly catches this for untracked plans. Cursor-provider plans A-E currently "pass" the detector only because they were committed as a single add (no --diff-filter=M history), which masks rather than fixes the violation.

Reproduction (during cursor-provider session 2026-05-19): both Spec D (cli-install-integration.plan.md) and Spec E (sync-target-output.plan.md) plans had filesystem mtime 2-3 minutes later than their first plan_task pending event in the lifecycle log. Once the plans were committed in d0f8303 and 199928a, the detector relaxed (relied on git history instead of mtime). The underlying violation persists.

## Design decision required

Two viable approaches:
  (a) Sibling .routing.md — /adev:route writes <plan-stem>.routing.md keyed by task ID; /adev:implement reads from it. Preserves human readability, adds one file per plan. Matches the .blockers.md pattern already adopted in commit 7e333fd for review BLOCK handling.
  (c) Lifecycle-log plan_task_routing event — /adev:route emits one event per task into the existing JSONL; /adev:implement reads it like other lifecycle state. No new file, but harder for humans to inspect routing decisions at a glance.

Variant (b) auto-commit-after-plan was rejected during /adev:debug — it silences the immutability detector via git history but still violates CON-8 prose ("read-only after authoring"), and forces an uncommitted-plans-impossible workflow.

Recommendation: variant (a) for consistency with the .blockers.md sidecar pattern.

## Files to change (variant a)

  - skills/route/SKILL.md:108-133 — Step 4: rewrite to write sibling .routing.md instead of mutating plan
  - skills/route/SKILL.md:168-174 — Integration with /adev:implement: point reader at sidecar
  - skills/route/SKILL.md:193 — Red Flag: tighten to "never modify the plan file"
  - skills/implement/SKILL.md — reader change: load routing from sibling .routing.md
  - .context-index/specs/features/agent-reliable-state-artifacts/plan-task-events.spec.md:50-58 — CON-8: enumerate .routing.md as a permitted peer artifact (alongside .review.md, .validate.md, .blockers.md)

## Migration of 5 already-mutated cursor-provider plans

Once the fix lands, the existing plans on the cursor-provider/cursor-adapter branch will have stale inline annotations. Affected:
  - .context-index/specs/features/cursor-provider/hook-config-generator.plan.md (Spec A)
  - .context-index/specs/features/cursor-provider/cursor-adapter.plan.md (Spec B)
  - .context-index/specs/features/cursor-provider/plugin-manifest-and-parity.plan.md (Spec C)
  - .context-index/specs/features/cursor-provider/cli-install-integration.plan.md (Spec D)
  - .context-index/specs/features/cursor-provider/sync-target-output.plan.md (Spec E)

Two migration options:
  (i) Extract: parse each plan, lift the **Routing:**/**Scores:**/**Rationale:** blocks into a new sibling .routing.md, rewrite the plan body without them, stamp the M-commit hash into manifest.yaml hygiene.plan_immutability.exempt_commits[]. Cleanest end state, more work.
  (ii) Leave as historical noise: do not rewrite. New /adev:route invocations on these plans would refuse to write (plan is locked), so any re-routing requires manual extraction. Simpler, but leaves the plans with inline annotations that future readers may mistake for the canonical format.

## Followups flagged in /adev:debug

  1. Draft an ADR titled "Plan-adjacent sidecar artifacts" documenting the .routing.md and .blockers.md sidecar pattern with rationale grounded in the authoritative-channel invariant. The pattern is now used twice (route + review BLOCK in commit 7e333fd) so a single ADR captures both.
  2. Extend lib/plan-immutability.mjs to catch the "mutate-then-single-add-commit" pattern by checking plan body for inline **Routing:** blocks when no sibling .routing.md exists. Would have caught Specs A-E despite their clean git history.
  3. Audit /adev:validate, /adev:review-specs, /adev:debug for any other plan-file writers — same invariant applies.

## History note

The original /adev:debug invocation that produced this diagnosis was filed in this session against issues that were subsequently lost when the shared tasks.json was rolled back externally. The diagnosis is preserved in the /adev:debug subagent transcript (agent ID affc19ea4ef7212c7) and in the retro at .context-index/hygiene/retros/2026-05-19-cursor-provider.md.

Re-filed on 2026-05-19 (consolidated from prior lost issue-525 + issue-528).

title: Resolve execution state across worktrees like the issue board already does
description:
Root cause established 2026-08-12 after two agents independently fixed the same p0 vulnerability an hour apart (PR #214 and duplicate PR #215, both for issue-582), and after a whole concurrent epic (epic-102, issues 568-581, PRs #210-#214) stayed invisible to a study pursuing the same goal. The issue board resolves storage via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (lib/issues/resolve-root.mjs) and IS shared across worktrees. Execution state does NOT: lib/execution-state.mjs reads <projectRoot>/.context-index/.execution-state.json, which is worktree-local. Measured live: /adev:work Step 1 reported status "idle" in this worktree while four epic-102 issues were in_progress and five PRs were open. Second, behavioural half: the board DID carry the signal (issue-582 was already in_progress) and nothing re-reads an issue at the moment work begins, so stale local knowledge won over the shared record.

Smallest change with the largest effect: point lib/execution-state.mjs at resolveStorageRoot() from lib/issues/resolve-root.mjs (already written, already tested, already handles the --git-common-dir case), or scan sibling worktrees and merge. Today the state scan is blind by construction, not by accident. Decide deliberately whether execution state should be SHARED (one lease per repo) or MERGED (per-worktree records, aggregated for display) — sharing changes semantics for legitimate parallel worktree work, which /adev:implement --parallel depends on.

RESOLVED 2026-08-13 (epic-107): Closed by 36f84fd6 (resolver) + a3687935 (the two shadow-path sites it exposed: session-capture read local while the writer wrote shared; migrateExecutionState guarded local and wrote shared, so a worktree run overwrote main live state).

title: work-tracking eval fixture generates pre-standardization spec names, so the reverse index is always empty
description:
ROOT CAUSE ISOLATED, and it is one line in a shell script.

tests/evals/work-tracking/setup-fixture.sh generates spec files with the
PRE-STANDARDIZATION naming — `login.md`, `widgets.md` — while
lib/source-manifest.mjs:145 requires the `.spec.md` suffix:

So `buildReverseIndex` walks the fixture, matches nothing, and returns an empty
map. Every assertion built on it fails.

PROVEN, not inferred. Against the generated fixture:
  buildReverseIndex(...) -> size = 0        (test expects 3)
After copying the two specs to `.spec.md` names, with no other change:
  size = 3
  lib/login.mjs        -> .../auth/login.spec.md
  tests/login.test.mjs -> .../auth/login.spec.md
  lib/drifted.mjs      -> .../dashboard/widgets.spec.md
Exactly the three pairs the test asserts.

The fixture content is otherwise correct — it declares source-manifest.files
properly. Only the filenames are stale, left behind by the spec-suffix
standardization (epic-48, closed). The fixture is generated and gitignored-in-
effect (0 tracked files), so nothing flagged it when the suffix rule changed.

FAILURES THIS ACCOUNTS FOR — 5 of 32 when the suite runs alone:
  builds correct reverse index from fixture specs
  drifted.mjs maps back to widgets.md via reverse index
  identifies claiming spec for drifted file via reverse index
  fully traced files are not false-positived
  unclaimed file count matches expected
plus the three parent describes (Scenario B Lifecycle Bypass Detection,
Scenario C Reverse Index, Scenario F Issue Chain Tracing).

WHY IT HAD NO ISSUE UNTIL NOW: it lives in the eval tier, which `npm test`
excludes (scripts/run-tests.mjs makes the tiers disjoint). It only surfaces under

to issue-591 (integration-sandbox) or issue-592 (token-budget). They belong to
neither — this is a third, previously unattributed bucket.

title: No concurrent-write protection on shared tasks.md — cross-session writes lose data
description: lib/issues/file-adapter.mjs _write() does a plain readFileSync → mutate-in-memory → writeFileSync sequence with no locking, no atomic rename, and no version check.  Observed failure mode (2026-05-11 during 0.25.0 reconcile session): Three concurrent Claude sessions on the same project directory mutated tasks.md. The background agent (in a separate session) created epic-72 and re-parented issues 274/374 — those changes were visible briefly on disk, then completely wiped by a subsequent write from a different writer that had read an earlier version. Other concurrent changes (epic-65/66/69 closure, epic-70 milestone move, issues 456-458 creation) survived. The pattern is unpredictable last-writer-wins lost-update behavior.  Impact: every multi-session scenario (worktrees, parallel agents, user-plus-agent edits) silently loses work. Issue board state cannot be trusted under concurrent access. This is structurally severe because the issue board is the canonical source of truth for plan/issue/epic state across the lifecycle.  Possible fixes (need spec discussion): 1. File lock via proper-lockfile or fs/promises advisory flock around _read+_write critical section. 2. Atomic write via temp file + rename, plus a version/etag check (compare-and-swap) — read returns a version token; write fails if disk version != staged version, triggering a re-read-and-retry. 3. Move to JSON-with-CAS or SQLite — both give atomicity for free and unblock the json-issue-board-adapter spec (issue-457).  Fits under epic-71 (Agent-Reliable State Artifacts). Probably the highest-priority structural fix in that epic since it underpins all other state-artifact reliability work.; Closed: Validated 2026-05-17 — all 15 AC pass, npm test green, 3 commits on feat/agent-reliable-state-artifacts/concurrent-write-protection branch. CAS implementation exceeds original spec guarantee (now unconditional via O_EXCL lock-file).

title: Artifact Frontmatter & Schema Hygiene
Surface domain extensions during adev init (extension picker / discovery hint)
description:
## Problem

A user installing adev into a new project sees only the bundled `software` domain. The framework has already moved non-software domains into installable extension packages (`extensions/data-engineering/`, `extensions/process-automation/`, both with validated specs PASS), and the install pipeline (`adev extension install <source>`) is fully implemented in `cli/index.mjs:956-997` and `lib/extensions/install.mjs`. But `adev init` (or the equivalent install wizard) does not mention extensions at all — there is no discovery surface telling the user that data-engineering, process-automation, or future domains are available.

Symptom: the user picks software-with-wrong-fit, or writes a custom domain from scratch (re-discovering `extends: software` + `.context-index/domains/<name>/` + `domain: <name>` in manifest.yaml), or simply does not realize extensions exist.

## Charter context

`.context-index/specs/features/domain-extensions/charter.md:29` *explicitly* lists "Auto-install during `adev init`" as out of scope for v1 of the extension work. The wording "for v1" was deliberate — that v1 was the content+pipeline; the install-UX bridge is the natural v2 follow-on. This issue is that follow-on.

## Recommended fix

Add an extension-discovery prompt to the init flow. Two implementation paths, ranked:

1. **First-party catalog with picker** *(preferred)*. After the providers prompt and before the context-index scaffold step, scan a known set of first-party extensions (start with the two that exist: `data-engineering`, `process-automation`). Present:
   ```
   Heading: Domain Extensions
   Select a domain extension to install (or skip for software-only):
     1. software (bundled) — general-purpose [default]
     2. data-engineering — pipelines, ETL, dbt, data quality
     3. process-automation — workflow automation, CI/CD orchestration
     4. skip
   ```
   On selection, call `installExtension(<path>, projectRoot, opts)` (the same function the CLI verb wraps). The first-party catalog can live as a small JSON manifest in `templates/` or embedded in `cli/index.mjs`. Multi-select also reasonable.

2. **Discovery hint only** *(minimal)*. After init completes, print a one-line note:
   ```
   Tip: To use a domain other than software, install an extension:
         adev extension install ./extensions/data-engineering
         adev extension install <git-url>
         (or browse: https://agentic-dev.org/extensions)
   ```
   No prompt, no install — just discoverability.

Option 1 fixes the UX gap; option 2 reduces it. Both close the report-symptom that prompted this issue.

## Scope

1. Decide between picker (option 1) vs hint (option 2). Picker recommended.
2. If picker: define the first-party catalog (which extensions ship as known options). Start with the two that exist in this monorepo.
3. Wire the catalog into `cli/index.mjs` init/upgrade flows.
4. Reuse `installExtension()` from `lib/extensions/install.mjs` for the actual install — no new install machinery.
5. Persist the choice in `manifest.yaml` (`domain: <name>` plus extension stamp via existing `readManifestStamps()` flow).
6. Update `skills/init/SKILL.md` to walk the user through the picker.
7. Update the install-completion message to confirm which domain extension (if any) was selected.
8. Test: integration test exercising init with each catalog choice.

## Acceptance criteria

- `adev init` surfaces available domain extensions to the user.
- User can select one (or skip) without leaving the init flow.
- Selected extension is installed via the existing `installExtension()` pipeline.
- `manifest.yaml` is stamped with the chosen domain and extension provenance.
- `adev upgrade` offers the same picker if no domain extension is installed.
- A new project where the user picks data-engineering has working `.context-index/domains/data-engineering/` after init (or whatever path the extension resolves to).
- The install-completion message shows the selected domain.

## References

- Charter (and out-of-scope note): `.context-index/specs/features/domain-extensions/charter.md:29`
- Install verb implementation: `cli/index.mjs:956-997`
- Install pipeline: `lib/extensions/install.mjs`
- Existing first-party extensions: `extensions/data-engineering/`, `extensions/process-automation/`
- Adjacent open issues: issue-447 (extract non-software domains), issue-448 (data-engineering package), issue-450 (remove from bundled templates) — those address packaging; this issue addresses discoverability/install UX, which they do not.
- Source of report: a user installing adev into a new project who only saw `software` and did not realize extensions were available.

title: A review verdict that cannot reach its requester is indistinguishable from a review that never ran
description: Observed live 2026-08-13 during epic-108 wave 2, twice, in the same session. Class: a review outcome is lost and NEITHER side sees an error. (1) Stranded verdict. A dispatched synthesized reviewer completed a re-review of hygiene-test-debt.spec.md rev 2 and returned PASS_WITH_NOTES, having verified all three round-1 blockers RESOLVED empirically against the real suite. It could not deliver that verdict to the session that requested it (SendMessage: 'no agent named general-purpose is reachable') so it returned the report one level up to the orchestrator. The requesting session, receiving nothing, reasonably concluded the review had been cancelled, wrote 'a re-review was deliberately NOT run' into the .review.md Disposition, and proceeded to implementation. The work was better-verified than its own record claimed. Recovered by hand in commit 18ee9e4b only because the orchestrator happened to be holding the report. At least three other nested agents in the same session hit the identical addressing failure (a plan review that returned Approved, a Task-1 implementation report, a spec-compliance PASS). (2) Same class, different mechanism, already fixed in ed84a277: /adev:review-specs SKILL.md emits 'adev report --type step --verdict BLOCK', which the verb rejects (PASS|PASS_WITH_NOTES|FAIL only), so the review step emitted 'started' with no terminal event. Silent because the validate gate checks 'implement', not 'review' — any later /adev:plan or /adev:review-specs on that spec would have blocked PERMANENTLY. That specific contract mismatch is issue-584; this issue is the general failure mode. Why P1: adev's entire gate model assumes a recorded verdict is a faithful record of whether review happened. Both failures break that assumption silently and in the UNSAFE direction — one loses a PASS (work looks less verified than it is, wasting effort), the other loses a BLOCK terminal (spec wedged forever). Directions worth considering: make a dispatched-review request carry a correlation id the requester polls for rather than relying on push delivery; have the report verb reject unknown verdicts LOUDLY at the call site rather than failing silently; and add a diagnostic for a lifecycle step that emitted 'started' with no terminal event within a run, which is the on-disk signature of both failures.

title: BeadsAdapter passes the .beads DIRECTORY as --db; br 0.2.22 requires the .db FILE, so every beads operation fails
description: Found 2026-08-13 attempting 'adev issues migrate --to beads --include-closed' on this repo (307 issues / 106 epics). The migration failed on the FIRST item and created nothing. REPRODUCTION: (1) br init -> creates a .beads/ DIRECTORY containing beads.db, beads.db-shm, and a .gitignore. (2) lib/issues/beads-adapter.mjs:29 sets this.dbPath = join(projectRoot, '.beads') -- the directory -- and line 54 passes it as ['--db', this.dbPath, ...args]. (3) Every br invocation then fails with: CONFIG_ERROR 'Refusing unsafe configured database leaf <database-authority sha256=...>: expected a regular file, not a symlink or special file'. VERIFIED the path is the whole cause, not the payload: 'br --db <root>/.beads create "plain test title" --type bug' fails identically to a title containing backticks and colons, while 'br --db <root>/.beads/beads.db create "migration probe title" --type bug --json' SUCCEEDS and returns a well-formed issue (id adev-plugin-ou0). MISLEADING SURFACE SYMPTOM worth noting for whoever picks this up: the migrate verb reports MIGRATE_PARTIAL_FAILURE naming the first issue it tried (here issue-582, whose title contains backticks and the word SECURITY), which reads exactly like a shell-quoting or injection bug in the title. It is not -- the adapter uses execFileSync with array args and never invokes a shell. Any title fails. Do not chase the quoting theory. LIKELY CAUSE: generational drift between bd (beads, Go) and br (beads_rust). A bd-to-br-migration skill exists in this environment for exactly this class of change, so the older bd probably accepted a directory for --db while br 0.2.22 requires a regular file. FIX: beads-adapter.mjs:29 should resolve the database FILE, e.g. join(projectRoot, '.beads', 'beads.db'), ideally probing for the actual db filename rather than hardcoding it, and should fail with a clear diagnostic when .beads exists but no db file is found. The path is currently hardcoded with no manifest override (tasks.db_path governs the storage ROOT via resolveStorageRoot, and does not reach this field). IMPACT: the beads backend is completely non-functional against br 0.2.22 -- not merely migration, but every create/update/close/list through BeadsAdapter. NO DATA WAS LOST in the failed attempt: 0 issues created, json board untouched at 307/106, manifest still tasks.backend: json, and the .beads dir was removed. A pre-migration board snapshot is committed at c3d4a875 on branch chore/board-migrate-to-beads.; Closed: ALREADY FIXED ON MAIN by commit 9dc95701 ("make the beads backend work against br 0.2.x"), which landed while this was being worked. Main resolves the *.db file inside .beads/ (preferring beads.db) and omits --db entirely when the workspace is uninitialized so br applies its own auto-discovery. Main also fixes two defects this issue never found: it canonicalizes the path via realpath because br refuses a symlinked parent and macOS /var -> /private/var breaks every call, and _runBr now surfaces stdout when stderr is empty (br reports structured failures as JSON on STDOUT, which is why the original error read as a bare "Command failed"). A local fix was written independently (branch fix/beads-adapter-db-path, commit 14f71cf8, 5 TDD tests) and is DISCARDED as redundant and strictly inferior; it survives in reflog only. Verified fixed: migration against main creates 310 issues + 106 epics with 0 errors.

title: milestone ship gates_pass auto-check broken — reads deprecated manifest.gates.test AND fails when populated
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-19 while running /adev:issues milestone ship 0.27.0. Two related defects in lib/milestones.mjs::evaluateShipCriteria (the gates_pass auto-check branch):

1. CONFIG-LAYOUT DRIFT: the check reads `manifest.gates.test` directly. The post-0.26.0 layout moved gate definitions to .context-index/governance/gates.yaml (see manifest.yaml line 123: 'The legacy top-level gates: block here is no longer read'). evaluateShipCriteria was not updated when the move landed. Reproduces with any milestone whose manifest follows the new layout — gates_pass fails with detail: 'No test command configured in manifest.gates.test' even when governance/gates.yaml correctly defines the test gate.

2. EXECUTION FAILURE WHEN POPULATED: workaround was to re-add `gates.test: "npm test"` to manifest.yaml. After that, gates_pass STILL fails with `passed: false, detail: ""` (empty stderr). The check uses `execFileSync("npm", ["test"], { stdio: "pipe" })`. Manual `npm test` from same shell returns 0 (3426/0/0 green), so the failure path is in evaluateShipCriteria's invocation — possibly buffer overflow on large stdout, PATH resolution under execFileSync, or signal-handling difference.

Blocks: /adev:issues milestone ship for any milestone using release-please/tag-only strategy with a real test suite. Workaround: `manual` strategy bypasses gates_pass (and skips release-please integration entirely).

Fix scope: (a) read `governance/gates.yaml` via the unified loader, OR (b) keep manifest.gates.test as the source but fix the execFileSync invocation. (a) is the right long-term fix per the post-0.26.0 architecture; (b) is the minimal patch.

Affects: lib/milestones.mjs::evaluateShipCriteria (gates_pass branch); skills/issues/SKILL.md milestone-ship documentation.
close_reason: Fixed in 610aa9ef. Reproducing the old branch found three failures, one worse than the reported crash: gates:{test:"a && b"} returned passed:true HAVING RUN ONLY the first command — a naive split(/\s+/) producing a FALSE PASS, so a milestone could ship on a gate that never fully ran. Gates now resolve through .context-index/governance/gates.yaml + mergeGates like every other consumer, and execute as argv via execFileSync with shell:false. Severity per the gates.yaml header; error-severity blocks the ship, warning-severity does not. Tests 104 -> 118 including two real-subprocess tests proving shell metacharacters stay literal. Required narrowing an over-broad architectural assertion that banned the parseYaml symbol as a proxy for "the milestone DOCUMENT is JSON" — the document invariant is still enforced three other ways, and the narrowed gate was verified to still bite.

title: Adopt a per-provider native-vs-plugin capability map: demote absorbed plumbing to adapters, do not delete it
description:
Two independent research artifacts reach this conclusion — agentic-frameworks-market-update-2026-08.md (recommendation 2, with a native-vs-plugin ledger) and skill-surface-simplification-audit-2026-08.md (§F platform note).

Claude Code now natively provides: persistent dependency-aware task lists across compaction/resume, SessionEnd transcript archival, worktree-isolated background subagents, TaskCreated/TaskCompleted/TeammateIdle gate hooks, /rewind checkpoints, always-loaded auto memory. The ledger marks .execution-state.json and the session-capture pipeline as "mostly redundant" ON THAT HARNESS.

The decision rule is the whole point and is easy to get wrong: adev is multi-provider. providers/{codex,opencode} have no equivalent of task persistence, auto memory, or worktree-isolated subagents. So absorbed plumbing must be DEMOTED TO A PROVIDER ADAPTER, not deleted — adev-owned state stays the portable default, and a per-provider capability map decides when the adapter delegates to native machinery.

Deliverable: the capability map itself (which provider has which primitive), plus the adapter seam that consults it. Every "delete the plumbing" issue in this epic should depend on this landing first, or they will delete portability.

title: Lifecycle reducer silently drops code_drift_detected / code_drift_cleared / spec_amended into unknownEvents
description:
Drift IS detected and IS written to the event log, but the canonical projection
throws it away — so every consumer reading currentState() is blind to drift the
system successfully recorded.

MECHANISM
  - CANONICAL_EVENTS (exported from lib/lifecycle-events.mjs) DOES include
    code_drift_detected and code_drift_cleared, so appendEvent's gate at
    lib/lifecycle-state.mjs:1444 accepts them and they land in the JSONL.
  - The reducer switch at lib/lifecycle-state.mjs:1449 has NO CASE for either.
    They fall through to the default at :1564 and are bucketed into
    unknownEvents. Same for spec_amended.

VERIFIED ON MAIN, not just the working tree — lib/lifecycle-state.mjs currently
carries uncommitted edits from concurrent work, so this was checked against the
committed file. A grep for a code_drift_detected case in the reducer on main
returns 0; the same grep over lib/lifecycle-events.mjs returns 1. An event the
writer accepts as canonical and the reducer treats as unknown is a contract
split inside one module.

LIVE INSTANCE: .context-index/lifecycle-state/graduated-rigor-tiers.jsonl records
a code_drift_detected event against skills/work/SKILL.md dated 2026-08-13.
currentState() on that spec reports only the specify step — the drift is
invisible in the projection skills actually consume.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE OBVIOUS: this is the mechanism behind the "only one
direction of drift is detected" complaint in issue-c9j36w. Both directions ARE
detected; one is dropped on the way out. Fixing the reducer may make the
proposed hygiene rule unnecessary.

Found by a read-only investigation agent while checking whether issue-c9j36w was
already resolved; independently re-verified against main before filing.
close_reason: Fixed. Root cause was not an oversight but a HALF-EXECUTED migration: jsonl-drift-events.spec.md Migration Step 0 required both canonical registration AND a documented variant row, and named the omission as the CON-4 blocker. The discriminators reached CANONICAL_EVENTS so appendEvent accepted them, but no reducer case and no spec row were ever written. Reducer now projects state.drift ({source, at, ts} | null, last-wins on detected, reset on cleared per Behavior 5, deliberately not an accumulating list because rev 3 rescinded multi-source history) and state.specAmendments[] (accumulating, mirroring specRevisions). status/currentStep untouched — both concerns are advisory, and a test asserts requireGate is byte-identical with and without drift. state.drift is documented as NOT authoritative for is-this-drifted, since the legacy fallback means a pre-migration spec can be drifted with zero events; frontmatter stays authoritative. Verified on the live graduated-rigor-tiers fixture: drift now projects, unknownEvents 0, status/currentStep unchanged. Tests 84 -> 95, 207/207 across nine lifecycle-adjacent suites. The recurrence guard is the strongest part: a test writes one bare line per CANONICAL_EVENTS member and asserts unknownEvents is empty, so any future canonical event without a reducer case fails immediately. Spec debt closed in the same change.

title: Issue-board ID allocation is not safe across git branches — two sessions minted the same issue-589
description:

title: gaming-gate EMPTY_ASSERTIONS false-positives on `it (` in comments and unbalanced braces in strings — blocks legitimate edits
description:
The EMPTY_ASSERTIONS detector in lib/test-strategies/gaming.mjs produces false
positives that BLOCK legitimate edits. It runs as a PreToolUse hard-blocking hook
(hooks/gaming-gate.sh, registered on the Write|Edit matcher), so a false positive
is not advisory — it stops the edit.

Hit live 2026-08-14 editing tests/cli/install-session-capture.test.mjs:

  BLOCKED: this edit introduces a new gaming violation
  {"patternId":"EMPTY_ASSERTIONS","line":551,"match":"it (",
   "message":"Test block contains no assertion calls"}

TWO INDEPENDENT DEFECTS, both confirmed by bisecting against the real detector.

DEFECT 1 — `it (` is matched inside COMMENTS.
Line 551 of that file is prose: "...so symlink the plugin's lib/ in and exclude it
(+ the post-commit-mode manifest) from `git add -A`." The substring "exclude it (" is
read as an it(...) test-block opener. Nothing strips comments before matching.

DEFECT 2 — brace counting is NOT STRING-AWARE.
An unbalanced `{` inside a string literal shifts every subsequent block boundary, so
the phantom block from defect 1 closes before reaching any assertion and is reported
as empty.

MEASURED, four variants of the same edit against detectSharedGamingPatterns():
  assertion string "(async()=>{ const fs = await import('node:fs')"   -> 1 violation
  same, plus a second assertion                                        -> 1 violation
  assertion string with NO brace: "const fs = await import('node:fs')" -> 0 violations
  assertion string with BALANCED braces: "(async()=>{ ... }"           -> 0 violations
The unmodified file scores 0. So the trigger is precisely an unbalanced brace inside
a string literal, landing after a comment that contains "it (".

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL FALSE POSITIVE. This detector exists to stop
agents from weakening tests. When it fires wrongly on a legitimate edit, the cheapest
path available to an agent is to reword the assertion until the gate goes quiet —
which is indistinguishable from the gaming it is meant to prevent, and trains exactly
the bypass habit issue-610 warns about for claim leases. A blocking gate with
false positives is worse than an advisory one.

DISCLOSURE: the immediate edit was landed using the brace-free assertion variant.
That is not a weakening — "const fs = await import('node:fs')" proves the payload
flowed through as literal data exactly as the original did — but it IS shaped by the
detector bug rather than by the test's needs, and that is recorded in a comment at
the site so the next reader knows why the fragment is written that way.

FIX: strip comments and string literals before pattern-matching and before brace
counting. A tokenizer-lite pass would close both defects at once. Add the two
variants above as regression fixtures.

ADJACENT, worth checking while in here: the same non-string-aware scanning likely
affects the other SHARED_PATTERNS in that module, since they share the block-boundary
machinery.

title: Document worker-vs-orchestrator fork pattern in skill frontmatter
description:
## Background
The single most important architectural pattern in adev — coordinator/orchestrator skills must NOT fork; worker skills SHOULD fork — is currently undocumented in any skill frontmatter and in using-adev. This caused ~50K tokens + several round-trips of wasted debugging during the 2026-05-15 lifecycle-artifacts charter build before commit f635b6a removed `context: fork` from `skills/build/SKILL.md`.

## The pattern
When invoked via the Skill tool, a skill with `context: fork` in its frontmatter runs in a forked subagent execution context that does NOT inherit the Agent dispatcher tool. This is correct behavior for WORKERS (which are themselves dispatched by an orchestrator via Agent and run in a clean subagent context with its own tool list). It is INCORRECT for ORCHESTRATORS like /adev:build, which need Agent to dispatch their pipeline steps.

## Current state (verified post-fix)
| Skill | Role | context: fork | Correct? |
|---|---|---|---|
| skills/build | orchestrator | removed (f635b6a) | yes |
| skills/implement | worker | present | yes |
| skills/deploy | worker | present | yes |
| skills/research | worker | present | yes |

## Proposed scope
1. Add an explanatory comment to each affected SKILL.md frontmatter declaring its role:
   - build: `# role: orchestrator — must NOT use context: fork (needs Agent dispatcher)`
   - implement/deploy/research: `# role: worker — context: fork is required for context isolation when dispatched by an orchestrator`
2. Add a section to skills/using-adev/SKILL.md documenting the pattern with examples and the failure mode it prevents.
3. Optionally add an integration test that asserts orchestrator skills do NOT carry `context: fork` and worker skills DO carry it.

## Reference
See .context-index/hygiene/retros/2026-05-15-lifecycle-artifacts-build.md action item #8 and the f635b6a commit message for full context.

title: Cache spec/charter/manifest reads in validate subagent
description:
Validate dispatches consume disproportionate tokens — averaged ~90-110K per spec across 13 checks during the lifecycle-artifacts charter build (~3x the per-implement cost). Most checks re-read the same spec, charter, and manifest files independently.

## Problem
Measured during 2026-05-15 lifecycle-artifacts charter retro:
- 11 validate dispatches × ~95K tokens avg = ~1.05M tokens
- 11 implement dispatches × ~25K tokens avg = ~275K tokens
- Validate is ~3x the cost of implement despite doing strictly less work (read-only verification vs. authoring code+tests)

Root cause: every check (1, 1.5, 1.6, 2-13) loads the same spec/charter/manifest files independently inside its own subagent context. No shared cache.

## Proposed scope
1. Audit which of the 13 checks actually need file content vs. could work from a single pre-parsed payload.
2. Add a read-once cache (spec body, charter, manifest, plan) at the validate subagent entry point and pass parsed data to checks.
3. Consider conditional check execution — skip Check 11 (UI) when no UI files exist; skip Check 9 (transitions) when no state-machine config; skip Check 7 (e2e) when no e2e suite. Signal these from the orchestrator rather than re-discovering per-subagent.
4. Consider whether some checks should be deduped or combined (e.g., Check 1 + 1.5 + 1.6 all read npm test output).

## Expected impact
- 30% token reduction conservatively → ~330K tokens saved per 11-spec charter
- Faster validate wall-clock (less LLM throughput on redundant reads)
- Cleaner check authoring contract (signature: (parsedContext) => result)

title: Research: unify quality gates and validation checks under a single logic
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-17 during /adev:validate scoping discussion on the incremental-artifact-writes spec. The user observed that we have two adjacent concepts with significant overlap and asked whether they should be one thing.

=== Current state (two parallel surfaces) ===

1. **Quality gates** (governance/gates.yaml) — tier-organized commands (fast | integration | e2e), each with kind (deterministic | probabilistic), severity (error | warning), required flag, triggers list (post-task | post-implement | pre-merge), group (smoke | full for e2e). Run by:
   - /adev:validate Check 1 (full tier sweep)
   - /adev:implement post-task hook (via gate triggers)
   - /adev:plan during planning context loading
   - CI directly (npm test, etc.)

2. **Validation checks** (governance/validate.yaml) — registry of checks with kinds (quality-gate | subagent-review | deterministic-check | observational), each with profile, fail-fast, after dependencies, severity. Run by /adev:validate only.

=== Friction points ===

- Check 1 of validation IS the quality-gate tier sweep — wrapper around governance/gates.yaml. Same logic, two entry points.
- Mental model gap: "what must pass before X" has no single answer. Quality gates? Validation checks? Transition gates (governance/gates.yaml transitions section)? All three?
- governance/ has three files (gates.yaml, validate.yaml, boundaries.yaml) that interact in non-obvious ways.
- check-set-restructure.spec.md already relocated 7 historic checks to other skills (review-specs, hygiene, reconcile, post-validate hook). The remaining 5–8 dispatched checks are a hybrid of "gate-like" and "review-like" work.
- Severity, fail-fast, and tier semantics are duplicated across gates.yaml (severity, tier) and validate.yaml (severity, fail_fast, after).

=== Possible unifications to study ===

A. **Single registry** — collapse gates.yaml + validate.yaml + transitions into one governance/checks.yaml with a uniform schema. Each entry declares: id, kind, trigger (when to run), severity, dependencies, command-or-skill-or-subagent.

B. **Layered registries with shared schema** — keep separate files for separation of concerns but make gates a subtype of validation-checks (kind: quality-gate already exists in validate.yaml). Validation checks include their own gates inline.

C. **Trigger-driven dispatcher** — separate from gates/checks files; introduce a "lifecycle event → check set" mapping (post-task fires gates with trigger:post-task; pre-merge fires all gates + all error-severity checks; etc.). Existing gate triggers list is the seed.

D. **Status quo + better docs** — accept the two-surface model and document the boundary clearly. Cheaper but doesn't reduce friction.

=== Research questions ===

- Are there projects with similar two-surface friction? (ESLint/Prettier vs Jest, or Bazel's test/build distinction, or pre-commit/pre-push hook divisions.) What did they pick?
- Does check-set-restructure's relocation logic suggest a deeper unification or argue against it?
- How much complexity is per-check kind (subagent-review needs profile/prompt; deterministic-check needs command; quality-gate needs tier/command/severity)? Could a uniform schema absorb all three without over-engineering?
- Migration cost — gates.yaml is well-established; breaking the surface risks invalidating existing projects' configurations.
- What's the user-facing benefit? One mental model? Faster CI? Fewer governance files? Clearer "what fails what" diagnostics?

=== Out of scope ===

- Implementation work — this is /adev:research first, then potentially spec → plan → implement.
- Lifecycle event log unification — that's already done by agent-reliable-state-artifacts.
- Existing ADRs covering this — none found; this would be a net-new ADR if unification is chosen.

=== Next action ===

Output: research artifact with the four options enumerated above, plus comparable patterns from ESLint/Bazel/pre-commit, plus a recommendation. If recommendation is "unify", file a follow-up spec; if "document the boundary", file a docs task.

description:
Two skills emit `adev report --type step --status completed` without a verdict, which causes the next skill's gate (`adev gate require`) to block until an operator manually re-emits the completed event with --verdict.

Affected skills:
- skills/specify/SKILL.md:465 — emits `adev report --type step --step specify --status completed` (no verdict). /adev:review-specs then blocks until verdict is re-emitted.
- skills/implement/SKILL.md:37 — emits `adev report --type step --step implement --status completed` (no verdict). /adev:validate then blocks.

Other skills (review-specs, plan, validate) DO emit a verdict on completion. The contract is therefore not uniformly applied.

Observed twice during 2026-05-17 lifecycle run on tree-sitter-repomap/non-code-reference-detection:
- After /adev:specify, /adev:review-specs blocked with: "step 'review' requires prior step 'specify' to be completed with PASS or PASS_WITH_NOTES (current: {status: completed, verdict: null})". Workaround: manually re-emitted specify completion with --verdict PASS.
- After /adev:implement, /adev:validate blocked with the same shape of error against the 'implement' prior step. Same workaround applied.

Fix (option A — chosen): make every skill emit a verdict on the completed event. specify is treated as PASS when it successfully writes the spec; implement is treated as PASS when the GREEN phase passes (which the skill already gates on internally). Two-line edits per skill.

Alternative considered (option B — rejected): relax the gate to accept `status: completed` without a verdict for steps that don't naturally produce pass/fail. Rejected because it weakens the gate's contract for the three steps (review, plan, validate) that DO produce verdicts.

Acceptance:
- skills/specify/SKILL.md and skills/implement/SKILL.md include --verdict PASS in their step-completed emission.
- A clean end-to-end lifecycle (specify → review → plan → implement → validate) succeeds without any manual verdict re-emission.
- /adev:validate is no longer blocked by an absent implement verdict.

Out of scope: changes to gate logic, changes to the failed-step verdict-emission path (specify/implement already correctly emit no verdict on failure — only the success path is affected).; Closed: PR #131 merged; specify/implement emit verdict on step completion

session-capture: add summary mode for SessionEnd captures instead of full verbatim transcript
description:
## Problem

`integrations.session_capture.capture: hook` (SessionEnd + PreCompact) writes a
VERBATIM dump of the conversation, not a summary. `fromTranscript()`
(lib/session-summary.mjs:165) walks every transcript line, extracts role + text,
and emits each turn under `### user` / `### assistant` with no condensation
step — no summarization, no truncation.

Users reasonably expect a "session log" to be a summary. The name of the
artifact directory (`.context-index/sessions/`) and the README's phrasing
("redacted markdown summaries") both reinforce that expectation.

## What is actually captured today

Captured: user message text, assistant message text, and `!command` stdout
(which arrives as a user message, so shell output lands verbatim).

Dropped: tool_use blocks, tool_result blocks (command output, file contents),
and thinking blocks — `extractMessageText` maps content blocks through
`b?.text`, so anything without a `.text` field is filtered out
(lib/session-summary.mjs:120).

`redactSecrets` (lib/session-summary.mjs:82) runs unconditionally, but it is a
fixed regex list (PEM blocks, bearer tokens, KEY=VALUE shapes). It catches
secret-SHAPED strings, not prose.

## Gap

There is no setting that combines the SessionEnd trigger with a condensed body.
The three modes are:

- `hook`        — SessionEnd/PreCompact trigger, full verbatim conversation
- `post-commit` — commit trigger, condensed body (subject/body, changed files,
                  tool counts)
- `off`         — nothing

A user who wants session-scoped capture (one file per session rather than one
per commit, which is the main win of hook mode) has no way to get a summary.
Their only route to condensation is to go back to `post-commit` and give up the
SessionEnd trigger — which is what this project just did.

## Proposal

Add a summarization option to hook mode. Sketch — exact shape open for design:

- a new knob, e.g. `integrations.session_capture.body: summary|transcript`
  (default `summary`), orthogonal to the existing `capture` trigger knob; or
- a fourth `capture:` value, e.g. `hook-summary`

Either way the summary body should record intent and outcome (what the session
set out to do, what changed) rather than the message log. The post-commit
renderer already demonstrates the target shape — Intent / Files changed /
Session activity — and could be adapted to a session-scoped input.

## Notes

- Reduces exposure surface for projects that track `.context-index/sessions/`
  in git. This repo is public and has 722 session files committed.
- Consumers to keep working: /adev:retro, /adev:status, /adev:hygiene,
  /adev:work all read `.context-index/sessions/`. Retro in particular parses
  the optional frontmatter (cost_usd, input_tokens, output_tokens, model,
  issue, epic) — a summary mode must keep emitting those.
- Spec to amend: .context-index/specs/features/session-awareness/hook-driven-capture.spec.md
  (Behavior 8 defines the SessionEnd render path; the Transcript redaction
  invariant at line 142 is adjacent).

## Minor defect found while investigating

`unregisterSessionCaptureHooks()` (lib/session-capture-installer.mjs:460) leaves
empty `"SessionEnd": []` / `"PreCompact": []` arrays in hooks.json rather than
deleting the keys. Functionally inert, but it means toggling hook mode on and
then off does not round-trip to the original file. Worth folding in or splitting
out.

   through it. The other 7 of 13 ARE frontmatter-first, so the verb works when

157/210 — a second independent instance of prose not holding the line.

be driven by new flags only a caller that already invokes the verb could pass, and
the 157-violation writer never invokes it. Also, the typical violator has no YAML
block to lift — its metadata is a prose blockquote (> **Date:**, > **Verdict:**),
and the 246 files containing a --- elsewhere are horizontal rules and table
separators, so auto-repair-by-lifting would corrupt bodies.

CORRECTED SCOPE — two follow-ups, neither in artifact.mjs:
  (a) A PreToolUse Write|Edit guard matching *.review.md / *.validate.md final
      paths. This is the only mechanism that makes the bad shape unproducible
      regardless of which writer runs, which is what "by construction" requires
      here. Model on hooks/plan-body-write-guard.sh (same _parse-stdin.sh +
      suffix-case + exit 2 shape); register in the existing "Write|Edit" matcher
      block at hooks/hooks.json:33.
  (b) Route skills/review-specs/SKILL.md Step 6b through .tmp + `adev artifact
      commit --kind review`. Provider mirrors exist under providers/codex/skills/
      and providers/opencode/skills/ and would need the same change.

artifacts alongside the verb's hasLeadingFrontmatter, exactly ONE file diverges —
output-personas/verbosity-axis-and-output-trimming.review.md passes the verb but
fires the diagnostic. Its frontmatter uses a `post-review-edit: |` block scalar:
valid YAML that the in-tree parseYaml mini-parser rejects. So the divergence is the
DIAGNOSTIC being over-strict, not the verb being under-strict, and wiring parseYaml
into the commit path would make the verb reject a valid artifact. The header comment
at lib/cli/artifact.mjs:48-51 ("so the writer and the diagnostic cannot disagree") is
inaccurate in that one direction — a doc nit, not a bug.

description:
SHIPPED DEFECT AFFECTING USERS, NOT JUST THIS REPO.

lib/domains/merge-gates.mjs:36 rejects any gate whose `command` is a shell string:

  INVALID_GATE: Gate '<id>' command must be an argv list (array), not a string — skipped.

That requirement landed in commit 9be9ffef and first shipped in **adev-cli-v0.25.0**.
Every gates.yaml authored before it — or hand-written since, following the old
docs — declares `command: "npm test"` and is DROPPED AT LOAD.

Nothing migrates it and nothing warns:

  - cli/index.mjs:292-297 scaffolds templates with `if (!existsSync(destPath))`,
    so an existing governance/gates.yaml is skipped entirely by install/upgrade.
  - No migration path in lib/migrate-state-artifacts.mjs or lib/cli/issues-migrate.mjs
    touches gate command shape.

MEASURED IN THIS REPO (2026-08-14). adev-plugin's own gates.yaml carried
`command: "npm test"`. Resolved through the real loader:

  BEFORE (string command): 0 gate(s) | INVALID_GATE
  AFTER  (argv list)     : 2 gate(s) | 0 warnings

So every /adev:validate Check 1 run in the adev repo itself, since 0.25.0, has
evaluated ZERO gates while reporting normally. Fixed here in commit 5d5b6c00;
users on their own scaffolds are still exposed.

This is issue-552's thesis ("all three repos wrote tests that never executed, and
adev never noticed") reproducing in the framework's own dogfood repo, and it is
independent evidence for that issue's p0.

PROPOSED FIX — one or more of:
  (a) a migration in `adev upgrade` that rewrites string commands to argv lists
      (a shell-string with metacharacters cannot be safely auto-split — those
      should be reported, not guessed);
  (b) at minimum, surface merge-gates warnings during install/upgrade instead of
      only at gate-resolution time, so a dropped gate is loud;
  (c) have `adev gate doctor` exit non-zero on INVALID_GATE (today it reports
      0 errors / 3 warnings for a config whose gate set is empty).

Note (c) matters most: gate doctor exists precisely to answer "do the declared
gates actually run", and a gate silently dropped at load is the case it should
never miss.

title: /adev:work has no worktree-isolated parallel batch mode — parallel agent work runs unisolated in one tree
description:
THE GAP. /adev:work has no parallel-agent mode at all. Its only use of the word
"parallel" is "parallel tool calls in a single round" for the Step 1 state scan.
Worktree-isolated parallelism exists only in /adev:implement --parallel, which is
driven by a plan's `## Parallelization` section and therefore unavailable for any
work that has no plan — bug batches, chores, research follow-ups.

So an operator who asks the front door to "batch these in parallel" gets whatever
the agent improvises. Today that was manual file-disjointness in ONE shared working
tree, which is --parallel's principle (file-disjoint groups) without its mechanism
(isolation).

MEASURED COST, 2026-08-14 session — ~10 agents across 4 waves, all file-disjoint:
  - an agent ran `git stash push/pop` on files other agents held, and raced a
    concurrent commit; two files came back staged. Nothing was lost, but only
    because the agent disclosed it and it was checked.
  - `npm test` stopped being a usable gate. One agent ran it three times and got
    three different results (2 fail / 2 different fails / 25 fail) because the
    modified-file set changed between two `git status` calls.
  - four separate agents spent tokens reasoning about edits that were not theirs,
    and each had to be told in its report which failures to ignore.
  - one agent reported the branch had "changed mid-session".
  - agents could not commit their own work, so every batch needed the orchestrator
    to verify and commit by explicit path.
File-disjointness itself held — no agent clobbered another's file. Everything that
broke is what isolation would have prevented.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT MAKES THIS NON-OBVIOUS. The naive fix — passing the harness's
`isolation: "worktree"` on each Agent dispatch — is explicitly FORBIDDEN by this
framework, at skills/implement/SKILL.md:460:

  "Do not pass isolation: 'worktree'. ... From inside an existing worktree, worktree
   isolation nests a new worktree inside the parent — the parent then captures it as
   untracked .claude/worktrees/agent-<id>/ content, and every per-task dispatch adds
   another level (8+ deep observed in field reports). Subagents that commit also
   defeat the harness's auto-cleanup contract, leaving the nested trees on disk
   forever."

So this capability cannot be "set the flag". It has to use adev-managed worktrees,
the same mechanism --parallel already uses.

THE PRIMITIVE ALREADY EXISTS AND RUNS STANDALONE:
  adev worktree <add|list|merge|remove|guard> [--slug <s>] [--base <ref>] [--no-ff]
                                              [--force] [--delete-branch]
It needs no plan. `adev worktree guard` already reports nested: true, which is the
detector for the nesting hazard above.

PROPOSED CAPABILITY — worktree-isolated batches from the front door:
  1. /adev:work gains a batch-dispatch mode that takes N independent work items
     (issue ids, not plan tasks) and runs each in its own `adev worktree add --slug`
     tree, then merges back deterministically via `adev worktree merge`.
  2. Reuse --parallel's existing machinery rather than inventing a second one:
     `adev parallel baseline` / `max-parallel` / `collision`, the RERUN_COLLISION and
     --fresh semantics, and the nested-worktree guard.
  3. Decide and document what the equivalence gate means here. For --parallel it is
     "a parallel run must be behaviorally equivalent to serial", enforced by the
     equivalence eval. Independent bug fixes have no such ordering guarantee, so the
     gate needs restating or explicitly scoping out.
  4. Keep file-disjointness as a PRECONDITION, not a substitute. Worktrees remove the
     interference; they do not make two agents editing the same file safe to merge.

GOVERNANCE: adding a mode to /adev:work is a skill-surface change and per CLAUDE.md
"Adding new skills to the lifecycle order" / skill-surface changes require human
approval. This should get a spec before implementation, not a direct patch.

RELATED: issue-547 (Parallel Implement, closed) shipped the worktree machinery;
issue-546 (Worktree Primitive, closed) shipped the verb. This issue is about making
the front door able to USE them for non-plan work.
