title: Chained git-hook wrapper fails open silently and embeds an absolute path; chaining guts tracked .githooks/ without warning
description:
Chained git-hook mode (`setupGitHooks()`, cli/index.mjs:385-473, wrapper generated by `buildChainedHook()` at cli/index.mjs:351-378) has three defects. It is reached whenever a project already has a foreign `core.hooksPath` (husky, lefthook, ...) at `adev install`/`adev upgrade` time — and it is the DEFAULT choice ("[1] Chain hooks", cli/index.mjs:402-406), so pressing Enter selects it.

Sibling of issue-uji735 (same install-flow area: the installer takes irreversible action ahead of, or instead of, the user's decision). Distinct defects — file separately, do not fold.

DEFECT A — the wrapper fails OPEN, silently.
buildChainedHook emits two guards:
  cli/index.mjs:361  if [ -x "$HOOK_DIR/<name>.adev" ]; then ... fi
  cli/index.mjs:371  if [ -x "$ORIGINAL" ]; then ... fi
  cli/index.mjs:376  exit 0
If either file is missing or merely loses its executable bit, the wrapper skips it and exits 0. No message, no non-zero exit. A hook that has been silently disabled is indistinguishable from a hook that passed.

What stops enforcing locally when this happens:
  - protected-branch blocking (commits straight to main)
  - conventional-commit-type validation
  - Author-type / Operator provenance trailer injection
  - the inline-Node policy check (pre-commit-no-inline-node)

Not hypothetical. Observed in this repo 2026-08-14: the `.githooks/*.adev` files were mode `-rw-r--r--` (NOT executable), which is exactly the state that triggers the silent skip — even though cli/index.mjs:438 chmods them 0o755 at write time. The exec bit does not survive every round trip (archive/restore, zip, some CI checkouts, Windows/WSL). The CI-side provenance gate would eventually catch missing trailers at PR time, but every local guard is already off by then.

Fix direction: a missing-or-non-executable `.adev`/original must be a loud failure (non-zero exit with a diagnostic naming the path and the fix), not a silent `exit 0`. If a fail-open escape hatch is wanted, it must be explicit and announced.

DEFECT B — the committed wrapper embeds a machine-specific absolute path.
cli/index.mjs:415  chainFromPath = resolve(cwd, existingHooksPath)   // absolute
cli/index.mjs:432  originalHookPath = join(chainFromPath, hookName)  // absolute
cli/index.mjs:370  the wrapper writes it literally: ORIGINAL="<absolute path>"

`.githooks/` is normally tracked, so that absolute path gets committed. On a teammate's machine or in CI the path does not exist, guard 371 fails, and (per Defect A) the wrapper exits 0 — so the project's ORIGINAL husky/lefthook hooks silently stop running for everyone except the person who ran the installer.

Fix direction: emit a repo-relative path resolved at run time from `$HOOK_DIR` / `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, never an absolute path from the installing machine.

DEFECT C — chaining mutates tracked files massively with no warning.
cli/index.mjs:437 copies the real hook body to `<name>.adev`; cli/index.mjs:445 then OVERWRITES the tracked `.githooks/<name>` with the ~26-line wrapper. In this repo that presented as 639 deleted lines across four tracked hooks (commit-msg -174, post-commit -169, pre-commit -133, prepare-commit-msg -210) plus four untracked `.adev` files.

The `created` array does report ".githooks/<name> (chained with <path>/<name>)", but nothing warns that tracked, committed files were just gutted. A user seeing that diff cannot easily distinguish it from repo corruption, and `git add -A` pushes stub hooks to the whole team.

Fix direction: warn explicitly that tracked hooks are being rewritten, show the scope, and state that `.adev` files must be committed alongside the wrapper (or gitignored) for chaining to work for anyone else.

SCOPE
- cli/index.mjs buildChainedHook() (351-378) — fail-closed guards, relative path resolution
- cli/index.mjs setupGitHooks() chaining branch (428-453) — user-facing warning about tracked-file rewrite
- Decide and document whether `.githooks/*.adev` is meant to be committed or gitignored; the answer determines whether Defect A is a portability bug or a local-only one
- Tests: wrapper behavior when .adev is absent, present-but-non-executable, and present-and-executable; assert non-zero exit + diagnostic for the first two
- Test: generated wrapper contains no absolute path

ACCEPTANCE
1. A missing or non-executable `.adev` hook causes a non-zero exit with a diagnostic naming the path — never a silent `exit 0`.
2. Same for a missing/non-executable chained original.
3. The generated wrapper contains no absolute filesystem path; chaining works from a fresh clone on a different machine.
4. Chaining prints an explicit warning that tracked hooks in `.githooks/` are being rewritten.
5. The commit/gitignore policy for `.adev` files is documented (docs/hooks.md) and enforced by the installer.
6. Tests cover all three guard states and the no-absolute-path invariant.

Found 2026-08-14 while diagnosing a working tree in which all four tracked hooks had been reduced to stubs with non-executable `.adev` siblings.

title: Auto-recover from stale tasks.json.lock (orphan-lock cleanup)
description:
The CAS layer in lib/issues/json-adapter.mjs acquires tasks.json.lock via O_EXCL before each write and releases it in the finally block. If the process is killed mid-write (SIGKILL, OS crash, container OOM), the lock file persists. Every subsequent CAS mutator then hits EEXIST → STALE_BOARD_WRITE_RETRY → bounded retry → STALE_BOARD_WRITE. The issue board becomes effectively read-only until someone manually deletes the orphan lock. The error message does not mention the lock file, making the failure hard to debug.

.gitignore now excludes the lock file (committed in ba44d3b on the concurrent-write-protection branch) so it cannot propagate via git, but in-place developer environments still need recovery.

Proposed mitigation: when _write encounters EEXIST on the lock acquire, stat the existing lock file. If its mtime is older than a configurable threshold (default 30 seconds; override via manifest.tasks.cas_lock_stale_seconds), treat it as orphaned, unlink it, and retry the acquire (without consuming a CAS retry budget slot). Log a one-time warning on the recovery path so users notice if it happens repeatedly.

Surfaced 2026-05-17 during PR review of concurrent-write-protection. Filed at user direction as a follow-up; not in scope for the original spec.; Closed: [object Object]

title: Author docs/cli-reference.md — agent-facing CLI verb reference for all 24 verbs
description:
## Problem

`adev help` shows 5 of 24 CLI verbs. The remaining 19 (gate, report, build-state, partial, heuristics, source-manifest, domain, context, verify, state, execution-state, preflight, prototype, artifact, issues, diagnose, etc.) are referenced only in scattered SKILL.md prose. Agents looking for verb signatures or argument shapes have to (a) grep `cli/index.mjs` for the dispatch table, (b) read multiple SKILL.md files, or (c) run `node cli/index.mjs <verb> --help` against guesses. None of these is a usable discovery surface.

Confirmed by a session audit (2026-05-20): the agent-load path (SessionStart hook → using-adev SKILL.md → CLAUDE.md → Context Routing table) contains zero pointers to a CLI verb reference. `docs/skill-reference.md` exists for the /adev:* skills but there is no equivalent for the underlying CLI verbs.

## Recommended fix

Create `docs/cli-reference.md` mirroring the format and tone of `docs/skill-reference.md`. One section per CLI verb, grouped by audience.

## Scope

1. New file `docs/cli-reference.md` with two top-level sections:
   - **User-facing verbs** (5): `install`, `upgrade`, `uninstall`, `extension`, `migrate`. These are the public surface invoked via `npx @adev-org/adev-cli <verb>`.
   - **Lifecycle / internal verbs** (~19): `gate`, `report`, `build-state`, `partial`, `heuristics`, `source-manifest`, `domain`, `context`, `verify`, `state`, `execution-state`, `preflight`, `prototype`, `artifact`, `issues`, `diagnose`, `init`, `status`, `help`. These are invoked from SKILL.md prose and by other CLI verbs; agents need them for orchestration.
2. Per-verb entry format: one-line description, full argument signature (flags + types + defaults), one example invocation, link to implementing module (`lib/cli/<verb>.mjs` or anchor in `cli/index.mjs`), cross-references to relevant SKILL.md files that invoke it.
3. Add `docs/cli-reference.md` to `docs/README.md` under the Reference section (next to `skill-reference.md`).
4. Update the `using-adev` SKILL.md's existing reference to drop the 'when present' qualifier once the file lands.
5. Tests: optionally add a script-based check that every verb in the `cli/index.mjs` dispatch table has a corresponding section in `docs/cli-reference.md` (drift guard). Can ship as a v2 follow-on.

## Acceptance criteria

- `docs/cli-reference.md` exists and documents all 24 verbs currently registered in `cli/index.mjs`.
- Each verb has: one-line description, full argument signature, at least one example, link to implementing file.
- Verbs are grouped into user-facing vs lifecycle/internal sections.
- `docs/README.md` lists the new file under Reference.
- `skills/using-adev/SKILL.md` qualification ('when present') is removed.
- Spot-check: an agent asked about a specific verb (e.g., `adev partial`) should be able to answer from the new doc without reading source.

description: Descoped from test-depth-policy at revision 6 (see its Scope Boundary section). That spec assigns and records a depth per task; nothing verifies the authored suite matches it. Amend immutable-handoff-block.spec.md so packet keys are task-scoped (not spec-slug-scoped) and conformance evidence is per-task, replacing the current one-packet-per-spec-slug scheme. adev:issues skill prose drops body field silently on json backend create()
description:
The /adev:issues skill's create-issue prose accepts a body/description argument from the user, but the json backend's IssueManagerInterface.create() silently drops any field except the canonical schema (id, title, status, priority, type, dependencies, notes, next_action, created, updated). The field is named "notes" in the adapter, not "description".

Repro (observed in this session while filing issue-483):
1. Invoke /adev:issues create with a multi-paragraph body argument.
2. Skill calls manager.create({ title, description, type, priority }).
3. The created issue persists with notes="" — the description body is dropped without warning.
4. A follow-up manager.update(id, { notes }) is required to attach the body.

Impact:
- User-supplied issue bodies (repro steps, acceptance criteria, links) are silently lost on first create.
- Agent must do a defensive create-then-update dance to attach any body, or the skill prose must teach the agent to use notes (not description).
- No error is surfaced — the silent drop is the worst failure mode for a write API.

Two valid fixes (orthogonal — both prose-level, no behavioral change to the helper):
A) Update skills/issues/SKILL.md to consistently use "notes" instead of "description"/"body" when describing the create arguments, and add an explicit note that the body field is named "notes".
B) Update the json adapter's create() to accept and normalize a "description" alias to "notes" (still write to the same column).

Recommend option A (prose-only, fewer surfaces to keep in sync).

Affected files (audit needed):
- skills/issues/SKILL.md — "Create Issue" section and argument descriptions
- Any other SKILL.md that invokes /adev:issues create (notably /adev:plan and /adev:implement which auto-create issues)
- lib/issues/json-adapter.mjs (or wherever create() lives) — confirm the dropped-field behavior

Discovered while filing issue-483 in the same /adev:debug session (2026-05-14). See also: issue-483 is the original build-state path-drift bug that exposed this one.

Acceptance criteria:
- skills/issues/SKILL.md create-issue arguments documented using the field name the adapter actually stores
- Cross-skill audit: every place that calls manager.create() uses the correct field name
- Optional: adapter logs a warning when an unknown field is passed to create() (defense-in-depth against the same class of bug)
close_reason: Fixed in 684a677b. Confirmed by direct probe that validateIssue dropped body/description silently. Fixed at the SHARED boundary in lib/issues/interface.mjs rather than one adapter, because the beads adapter calls it too and was losing bodies identically. body/description now resolve as aliases of notes, which is what they already are everywhere (beads writes notes as --description). The conflict rule is deliberately ASYMMETRIC: two aliases disagreeing with no notes throws, but a non-empty canonical notes beside a disagreeing alias wins silently — because a symmetric throw BROKE adev issues migrate, since update() bypasses validateIssue and pre-fix boards carry stray keys that projectIssueForCreate replays through create(). That abort was reproduced and fixed both ways. 21 new tests asserting through a FRESH adapter; 540 board tests pass. Adjacent gap filed as issue-80m9s2: validateEpic has no notes field at all.

title: Implement Stage-2 review loop is unbounded ("Repeat until approved") while every sibling loop caps at 3
description:
skills/implement/SKILL.md:577 — "Critical or Important issues: The implementer fixes them. The reviewer reviews again. Repeat until approved."

No attempt cap, no convergence check, no escalation. Sibling loops (plan reviewer, implement Stage 1, implement visual) all cap at 3. The MAST failure taxonomy (Berkeley, NeurIPS 2025) catalogues this exact class as "step repetition without progress" and finds most agent failures are organizational rather than model-capability.

Fix: cap the loop and route the cap-trip through lib/loop-convergence.mjs verdicts (NO_PROGRESS / REGRESSED / BUDGET_EXHAUSTED) rather than a bare retry counter. The research also notes retry budgets are hardcoded prose strings ("maximum 3") in three places and should be config-backed per loop, like build.max_review_retries already is.

From .context-index/research/harness-simplification-study.md Part 3, "Loop inventory".

Source: 2026-08-14 research-vs-board audit. Claim re-verified against the codebase at that date, not taken from the research artifact alone.
close_reason: Fixed in 11b179d7. skills/implement/SKILL.md Step 2g no longer says "Repeat until approved": capped at 3 cycles, matching the sibling Stage 1 and visual loops, with each cycle routed through lib/loop-convergence.mjs rather than a bare counter. That required a new rule that finding ids be stable and reused across cycles — without stable ids NO_PROGRESS and REGRESSED are undecidable, which is presumably why the loop was unbounded. Terminal outcomes reuse build vocabulary (LOOP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED / LOOP_NO_PROGRESS / LOOP_REGRESSED) so one grep finds both loops. Escalation states plainly that Stage 2 has NOT passed. Budget hardcoded at 3 because no implement.max_review_retries knob exists; a config-backed budget mirroring build.max_review_retries is named as a follow-up. 11/11, no inline-Node introduced.

title: Bind issues to branch and PR so "is someone doing this?" is answerable offline
description:
Root cause established 2026-08-12 after two agents independently fixed the same p0 vulnerability an hour apart (PR #214 and duplicate PR #215, both for issue-582), and after a whole concurrent epic (epic-102, issues 568-581, PRs #210-#214) stayed invisible to a study pursuing the same goal. The issue board resolves storage via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (lib/issues/resolve-root.mjs) and IS shared across worktrees. Execution state does NOT: lib/execution-state.mjs reads <projectRoot>/.context-index/.execution-state.json, which is worktree-local. Measured live: /adev:work Step 1 reported status "idle" in this worktree while four epic-102 issues were in_progress and five PRs were open. Second, behavioural half: the board DID carry the signal (issue-582 was already in_progress) and nothing re-reads an issue at the moment work begins, so stale local knowledge won over the shared record.

Board items already carry spec_ref; add branch and pr, written when work starts and when a PR opens. Makes ownership answerable without the network and gives /adev:status and /adev:hygiene a real ownership view. Precedent that the repo can hold contributors to commit-level metadata: the commit-msg hook already blocks commits touching source-manifest-tracked files without a Spec: trailer (it fired twice during this session).

/adev:validate emits no lifecycle events (no gate, no started, no completed)
description:
Surfaced by lifecycle-event audit on 2026-05-17 (LIFE-1, LIFE-3). skills/validate/SKILL.md Step 0a uses inline-Node imports of currentState/requireGate/resolveGateMode/reportStep instead of `adev gate require --skill validate --spec

` and `adev report --type step --status started`. Worse, no completion event is emitted — the section structure jumps from Check 11 to Overall Status to After Validation without ever calling `adev report --type step --step validate --status completed`. Consequence: after /adev:validate runs, the lifecycle log shows lifecycle_step:validate started with no terminal event. Any future skill that gates on validate completion would block permanently. Same shape of bug as issue-508 but for a different skill. Fix: 1. Replace the Step 0a inline-Node block with `adev gate require --skill validate --spec

` + `adev report --type step --step validate --status started`. 2. Add a final emission step that calls `adev report --type step --step validate --status completed --verdict ` where aggregate is PASS / PASS_WITH_NOTES / FAIL based on the consolidated check results. Acceptance: - /adev:validate runs end-to-end without inline-Node in its critical-path gate logic. - Lifecycle log after a validate run contains both lifecycle_step:validate started AND step_completed:validate with a verdict. - Manual verification: a fictional downstream skill calling `adev gate require --skill ` after validate does not block.; Closed: PR #132 merged; validate skill emits canonical lifecycle events
